items.ai_summary: GitBook disclosed that a highly targeted attack using AI agents gained unauthorized access to some of its infrastructure credentials, exposing potentially sensitive API tokens and integration secrets and prompting it to revoke customer tokens while crypto projects like PancakeSwap relocated their documentation.
items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz

metadata.background_en: GitBook is a documentation platform that combines a wiki-style editor with Git-based version control, and crypto projects rely on such platforms to publish technical explanations and developer guides. Its disclosure does not establish that GitBook's own AI products were responsible for the intrusion. The company kept publicly available documentation reachable through cached copies while its underlying systems were down.
metadata.background_zh: GitBook 是一个将 wiki 式编辑器与基于 Git 的版本控制相结合的文档平台，加密项目依赖此类平台发布技术说明和开发者指南。GitBook 的披露并未证实是其自家 AI 产品导致了此次入侵。在底层系统下线期间，该公司通过缓存副本让公开可读的文档保持可访问。
metadata.detailed_summary_en:
GitBook disclosed that a "sophisticated, highly targeted attack using AI agents" gained unauthorized access to some of its infrastructure credentials at 7 p.m. Central European Time on November 2. The documentation platform, widely used by crypto projects, took authentication-gated sites offline, revoked personal API tokens and urged customers to replace connected credentials.

GitBook's connections to customer accounts and external services mean the blast radius extends to crypto teams' integration tokens, Git Sync secrets and API tokens. PancakeSwap responded by temporarily taking its documentation offline before moving it off the platform, while saying its own systems were not compromised.

GitBook said its investigation found no evidence that hosted content was modified, and that potentially exposed data includes integration tokens, Git Sync secrets, API tokens and questions submitted to its AI assistant. By Tuesday afternoon the company said its application, API and published documentation were accessible again, though some services could remain degraded; it has not explained how the attacker used the AI tools, which AI systems were involved, or how the credentials were obtained.
metadata.detailed_summary_zh:
GitBook 披露，一起“使用 AI 智能体的复杂、高度定向攻击”于欧洲中部时间 11 月 2 日晚 7 点未经授权访问了其部分基础设施凭证。这家被加密项目广泛使用的文档平台下线了需登录访问的站点，撤销了个人 API 令牌，并敦促客户更换已连接的凭证。

GitBook 与客户账户及外部服务的连接意味着影响范围波及加密团队的集成令牌、Git Sync 密钥和 API 令牌。PancakeSwap 的回应是先暂时下线其文档，随后将其迁出该平台，同时表示自身系统并未被入侵。

GitBook 表示调查未发现托管内容被篡改的证据，可能暴露的数据包括集成令牌、Git Sync 密钥、API 令牌以及提交给其 AI 助手的问题。公司称截至周二下午其应用、API 和已发布文档已恢复访问，但部分服务在恢复期间仍可能降级；它尚未解释攻击者如何使用这些 AI 工具、涉及哪些 AI 系统，以及凭证是如何被获取的。
metadata.market_impact_en: The channel here is credential and supply-chain risk rather than price: teams that connected GitBook to repositories, deployment pipelines or external services face potential exposure of integration and API tokens until those secrets are rotated. Documented migration off the platform by projects like PancakeSwap signals an operational, not a market-wide, disruption.
metadata.market_impact_zh: 这里的传导渠道是凭证与供应链风险，而非价格：曾将 GitBook 连接到代码仓库、部署流水线或外部服务的团队，在相关密钥完成轮换之前面临集成令牌和 API 令牌可能暴露的风险。像 PancakeSwap 这样的项目将文档迁出平台，表明这是一次运营层面的扰动，而非全市场范围的冲击。

items.ai_summary: Simon Willison demonstrates that a locally run Qwen 3.8 27B can interpret raw model weights, extending the recent Weight-Space Programming findings beyond frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra.
items.author: Simon Willison

metadata.background_en: Weight-space programming refers to a general-purpose LLM reading, interpreting and directly writing another neural network's weights without gradient descent or a training loop; the term was coined in the Takehi et al. paper, which the authors classify as a blog post. GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's frontier model, released to approved users on September 3, 2026. Qwen 3.8 27B is an open-weight dense vision-language model from Qwen built on the Qwen3.5 architecture.
metadata.background_zh: 权重空间编程（Weight-Space Programming）指通用大模型在不使用梯度下降或训练循环的情况下，读取、解读并直接写入另一个神经网络的权重；该术语由 Takehi 等人的论文提出，作者本人将其归类为博客文章。GPT-6 Astra 是 OpenAI 的前沿模型，于 2026 年 9 月 3 日向获批用户开放。Qwen 3.8 27B 是 Qwen 推出的开放权重稠密视觉语言模型，基于 Qwen3.5 架构构建。
metadata.detailed_summary_en:
Simon Willison reported that Qwen 3.8 27B, running locally on his laptop, could interpret raw model weights in a replication of an example from the paper "Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights" by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab. That paper had demonstrated the capability with frontier models, specifically GPT-6 Astra.

The demonstration indicates that no-tools weight reading is not confined to frontier systems such as GPT-6 Astra, since an open-weight model running on a laptop reproduced one of the paper's examples. It remains an exploratory blog-post replication rather than a formal result or peer-reviewed finding.

The paper's first experiment trained four neural networks to play 10x10 grid versions of Breakout, Pong, Pac-Man and Freeway, then supplied the weights as floating-point numbers to an LLM with the instruction that it had no tools, no code execution and a single response to identify which game each network was trained on. Willison focused on this no-tools question, noting that critics Matthew Honnibal and Sean Goedecke disputed the paper's framing of code-assisted model editing.
metadata.detailed_summary_zh:
Simon Willison 报告称，他在自己笔记本电脑上本地运行的 Qwen 3.8 27B 能够解读原始模型权重，复现了 Rikiya Takehi、Jayden Teoh、Alex Zhang 与 Omar Khattab 合著的论文《Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights》中的一个示例。该论文此前是以 GPT-6 Astra 等前沿模型展示这一能力的。

这一演示表明，无需工具即可读取权重的能力并不局限于 GPT-6 Astra 等前沿系统——一个在笔记本上运行的开放权重模型复现了论文中的一个示例。不过它仍属于探索性的博客复现，而非正式成果或同行评审结论。

论文的第一个实验训练了四个神经网络，让它们玩 10x10 网格版的 Breakout、Pong、Pac-Man 和 Freeway，随后把权重以浮点数形式交给大模型，并说明模型没有工具、不能执行代码、只有一次回答机会，要求其判断每个网络是为哪款游戏训练的。Willison 聚焦于这个“无工具”问题，并提到批评者 Matthew Honnibal 与 Sean Goedecke 对论文将借助代码编辑模型的做法归入同一概念提出质疑。
metadata.market_impact_en: The result concerns open-weight model research and local inference rather than any token or protocol, so there is no direct transmission to crypto assets; any effect would run only through sentiment around open-weight and decentralized-AI narratives. It is an interpretive demonstration, not a product or network change.
metadata.market_impact_zh: 该成果属于开放权重模型研究与本地推理范畴，并不涉及任何代币或协议，因此对加密资产没有直接传导路径；若有影响，也仅通过围绕开放权重与去中心化 AI 叙事的情绪面体现。它是一项解读性演示，而非产品或网络层面的变更。
